read: [00:00] Medi 'Right. Okay.' .. [1:04:26] CHAT Amal 'enbasa6tellak / enbasa6etlak' - all 921 turns, lines 1-923, read in order
coverage_note: 00:00-06:26 is English chat about a song; Amal's Arabic there is redacted as [foreign language], so the 03:22-03:57 words (loaf, yard) cannot be recovered - only two asked-rows written from his Latin (balad/bilad, Sakit). 06:26-10:49 is the only speaking stretch (date, time, weather, clothes). 11:13-1:00:35 is a listening drill: Amal says a sentence, Medi gives the English - so most rows are mode=listening and 'wrong' is his English reading. His Arabic in the drill is Latin and often garbled by the engine: Kamara / Kamamara / Tawamara = kaman marra / tani marra ('again', not errors); Bisar, bizat, Ma bistah, Bin hafi bin, Namaste, Basatu shu, Mao, ume mit as, Ume safulu, 'My choose Aloo' are garbled echoes of her line and were skipped. [07:26] 'ألفين تنين وتلات' is probably the engine's rendering of tentain u tult (she said صح) - two low/medium rows written from her chat spelling. خندرة (10:31) for كندرة and بيكميس (10:08) for قميص treated as S4/transcription, not vocab. [35:10] is stray background speech (library). [58:36] 'the gatherings' for بالعزومة not written: her sheet glosses عزومة as 'house gathering / invitation'. Chat lines lag 30-120 s; used as fixes only where they differ from what he said.

rows.medi_said: This is it today. تسعة عشرين.
rows.why: He built 19 as nine-twenty (تسعة عشرين); she prompted '19.', he moved to MSA تسعة عشر (06:42), and she recast her form تسعطاش at 07:12 (sheet: nineteen | tese3ta3sh | تسعتاش) - a wrong form of a number he knows, so tier 2.

rows.medi_said: تسعش ستة.
rows.why: The date is 19 of the 9th month; he said ستة (six) for the month at 06:59 and again at 07:10, she queried 'ستة؟' (07:04) then recast تسعطاش تسعة, and the chat confirms tes3a - a wrong number word, tier 1.

rows.medi_said: um, ألفين وسبعة عشرين.
rows.right: ألفين وستة وعشرين (best reading - the year 2026)
rows.why: Asked 'إيش من؟' (of which month) he answered with a year, and the year he gave has seven where 2026 needs six and the tens-form is off; he repeated it at 07:03 and she only steered him back to the month (19 شو؟), so no signal - B row, my reading.

rows.medi_said: ألفين تنين وتلات.
rows.why: Clock time takes the feminine number (sheet: it's 2:01 | Elsa3a tentain u d2ee2a); he said masculine تنين for 2:20, she said صح aloud but typed tentan u tult in chat; the engine's ألفين is probably a mishearing, so medium.

rows.medi_said: ألفين تنين وتلات.
rows.why: For 'twenty past' he said تلات (three) where the word is تلت (a third; sheet: third | Tult | تلت); her chat spells tult; low because the engine may have written تلات for his tult.

rows.medi_said: بتغي-- بتغير كتير. No, بتغير كتير. It's masculine.
rows.chat: el-jaw el-yoam t8ayyar kteer u shob mish m8ayyem
rows.why: He meant 'the weather changed a lot' (past) but used the b-present بتغير; she asked 'It changed?' (07:56) and named it 'تغير، no be'; he agreed 'past tense, you're right' and said تغير كتير at 08:18.
rows.english: The weather changed a lot today.

rows.medi_said: مش مغي-- مغاير معي.
rows.chat: el-jaw el-yoam t8ayyar kteer u shob mish m8ayyem
rows.why: He wanted 'not cloudy' and produced the non-word مغاير معي; her chat line spells the sentence with mish m8ayyem (sheet: the weather is cloudy | El-jaw m8ayyem | الجو مغيم).

rows.medi_said: أب-أب المـ-امبارح. أب المامبارح or أب الامبارح? أب الامبارح.
rows.amal_said: قبل امبارح or أول امبارح some people say.
rows.why: For 'the day before yesterday' he built أب الامبارح (a non-word, with an extra el-) and asked which version was right; she gave قبل امبارح / أول امبارح; he repeated أب الامبارح at 09:04 and she let that pass.

rows.medi_said: شو يعني ريحة؟
rows.why: Didn't-know: after her ريحة المطر حلوة he asked what ريحة means; she repeated it and he got 'the smell' (sheet: smell | ree7a | ريحة).

rows.medi_said: بلوز، uh، أبيض. أبيض؟ بيض؟ أبيض.
rows.chat: el-yoam balbes 2amees rasmi abyad u ban6aloan azra2 8aame2 u kundara binniyye
rows.why: بلوزة is feminine (sheet: shirt / blouse | Blooze | بلوزة) so the colour must be feminine; he wavered أبيض/بيض and settled on masculine, she recast the feminine (engine: بيضة); he then switched the noun to قميص رسمي, which is why her chat has abyad.

rows.medi_said: uh، أزرق، uh، كمي
rows.chat: el-yoam balbes 2amees rasmi abyad u ban6aloan azra2 8aame2 u kundara binniyye
rows.why: For 'dark blue' he trailed off on كمي and she supplied غامق (sheet: dark (color) | 8aameq | غامق); low because كمي may be a sound slip on غامق (غ→ك, dropped ق), which S4 would make pronunciation rather than vocab.

rows.medi_said: Uh, Lisa ma-- Or matahammasi Lisa.
rows.why: She asked him to say 'don't be excited yet'; he produced ma ta7ammasi (the make-form, 'don't excite someone') without the reflexive ت of tet7ammasi ('don't get excited'); she recast ما تتحمسي لسه and later typed it.

rows.medi_said: Uh, bizah.
rows.amal_said: زهقان. [تضحك] Of course it's that's it. It's بس زهق، زهق.
rows.why: She asked 'what's bored?'; he gave the verb بزهق ('that's boring', she said) instead of the adjective زهقان (sheet: bored | Zahqaan | زهقان vs boring / causes boredom | beyzahheq | بيزهق) - a verb used for a state word, tier 2 (B15 territory), and he then guessed zar'a before she supplied it.

rows.medi_said: Shufik. Bye.
rows.why: Echoing her أشوفك he dropped the person prefix (shufik is the bare stem / feminine imperative), so 'see you' lost its I-form; she did not react - B row.

rows.medi_said: Does balad mean like bilad? Like, balad.
rows.amal_said: [foreign language] , [foreign language] is one, [foreign language] is multiple.
rows.right: بلد (one) / بلاد (countries) - her Arabic redacted in the transcript
rows.why: Didn't-know from the song talk: he asked whether balad relates to bilad and she explained one vs many (02:18 'another way of saying countries'); not on her sheet (country | Dawle | دولة only), so tier 0 asked.

rows.medi_said: Does it come from, like, Sakit?
rows.amal_said: No, it's from [foreign language] . [foreign language] is a yard, house yard.
rows.right: her word for yard (redacted as [foreign language])
rows.why: Didn't-know: he guessed the root of a lyric word and she said no and taught the word for house yard; her Arabic is redacted so the target cannot be quoted - low.

rows.medi_said: So it's سكرت, right? ... It's صورت. There's no preposition.
rows.amal_said: Is it did you take a photo or did you get-- did you take a photo of yourself؟ Like, did you get photographed؟ Which one is it؟
rows.why: She said اتصورت؟; he read it as the make-form صورت 'you took a photo' (engine first wrote سكرت), she prompted took-vs-got until he gave 'I got photographed' (12:10).

rows.medi_said: you are tired of me.
rows.why: She said تعبتني (make-form + me); he read the get-form تعبت مني; she said no, then also prompted present vs past (13:09) until 'You tired me' (13:10).

rows.medi_said: Why did you break it? Why did I break it?
rows.why: She said ليش خربته؟; he read 'break', she pushed 'which break is this?' (13:54, 14:13) until he reached 'ruin' and, asked for the physical break, fumbled 'back sir' before she supplied كسر.

rows.medi_said: Why did you smile to a male or why did she smile?
rows.right: why do you smile / why are you smiling (بتضحك)
rows.why: ليش بتضحك؟ carries the b-present; he read it as past 'did', she prompted did-or-do and he fixed to 'Why do you smile? Present tense' (15:58).

rows.medi_said: Oh, you said... Okay, I was sad.
rows.right: I got bored / you got bored (زهقت)
rows.why: She said زهقت; he heard زعلت and gave 'sad' (also first asked if it was the inflict form, 16:26); she said زهقت مش زعلت and he fixed to 'bored' (16:52).

rows.medi_said: They had fun or they enjoyed?
rows.amal_said: آآآ. Close بس that would be انبسطوا. انبسطوا
rows.right: you (pl) - انبسطوا as she meant it (her chat vowels enbes6u read as the plural command 'have fun')
rows.why: He read 'they'; she said close-but and re-said the word, he switched to 'you guys enjoyed' (18:19) and she moved on; the chat spelling enbes6u (not enbasa6u as at 1:02:22) suggests the imperative, so the exact target is uncertain - low.
rows.english: Have fun, you all / you all had fun

rows.medi_said: What boring hap-- What happened boring?
rows.why: She said اللي صار بيزعل; he heard بيزهق and read 'boring'; she said no, بيزعل مش بيزهق, and he fixed to 'what happened is sad' (20:39).

rows.medi_said: Uh, what you did is angry.
rows.amal_said: مم. ممتاز. Let me write this one.
rows.right: makes (people) angry / is angering (بيعصب) - my reading
rows.why: بيعصب is the make-form (it angers); he rendered it as the state 'is angry' and she accepted with ممتاز - no signal, B row.
rows.english: What you did makes one angry.

rows.medi_said: He will not, he will not bore you.
rows.amal_said: Very close. أزهقك، not يزهقك. أزهقك.
rows.why: ما راح أزهقك has the I-prefix; he heard the he-form يزهقك; she said أزهقك not يزهقك and gave 'I won't bore you' (22:28); he then wandered into 'he will not be bored of you' and she supplied ما راح يكون زهقان منك (23:03).

rows.medi_said: What is the difference between he bored and I, uh, without the B, I am boring, I bore you, I bore?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say 'I bore (people)' and she supplied أنا بزهق (sheet: i bore / make people bored | Ana bazahhe2 | بزهِّق); he practised azah-eh / azah after it.

rows.medi_said: Were you sad from what happened?
rows.amal_said: Very close. بس مش sad. انزعجتي.
rows.why: She said انزعجتي من اللي صار؟; he read 'sad' (زعل); she said مش sad, انزعجتي, and he fixed to 'annoyed' (24:22).
rows.english: Did you get annoyed by what happened?

rows.medi_said: so don't be tired of me.
rows.amal_said: That's ما تتعبي مني. ما تعبيني.
rows.why: ما تعبيني is the make-form + me; he read the get-form (ما تتعبي مني); she named the difference and gave 'Don't tire me' (25:04), he repeated 'don't make me tired'.

rows.medi_said: They ruined the world?
rows.why: He read الدنيا literally as 'the world'; she prompted 'remember what it means?' and he fixed to 'they ruined everything' (26:07), which she confirmed.

rows.medi_said: She laughed at him.
rows.why: ضحكت علي ends in the -me ending on the preposition; he read عليه 'at him'; she recast علي, he fixed to 'at me' and admitted 'I'm never gonna get LA and LAE' (26:44).

rows.medi_said: Who was he mad with you-- at you? I don't... This doesn't make sense.
rows.amal_said: What's ضايقك؟ ... So is it ضايق or it's ضايقة to be upset؟
rows.wrong: Who was he mad with you-- at you
rows.right: who made you upset / who upset you (مين ضايقك)
rows.why: He read ضايقك as 'be mad at' and as the get-form; she prompted ضايق vs تضايق (27:56) until he said 'daya is to make someone upset ... who made you upset' (28:17).

rows.medi_said: Don't be angry at me or don't make me angry.
rows.why: For ما تعصبني he offered both the get-reading ('don't be angry at me' = ما تعصب علي) and the right make-reading; she picked 'don't make me angry' - low because he had the right one in his pair.

rows.medi_said: So basat is I was happy.
rows.why: She said بسطه (make-form + him); he read the get-form 'I was happy' and took the ـه for a preposition (32:26); she prompted 'So بسطت first' then 'I made', he fixed to 'I made him happy' (32:46).

rows.medi_said: You guys...
rows.why: بينبسطوا لما يشوفوني is they-form; he started 'You guys'; she repeated the verb and he fixed to 'they are happy when they see me' (33:41).
rows.english: They are happy when they see me.

rows.medi_said: Yeah, they apologized. Present tense. Can I...
rows.why: هما اتأسفوا مني is past (no b-); he labelled it present; she said لأ, اتأسفوا not بيتأسفوا, and he conceded 'I said it with the first tense' (39:14).

rows.medi_said: I ruined the, the s- the trip. ... Oh, khirbat. Uh, she ruined the trip.
rows.amal_said: Are you sure؟ I ruined؟ ... No؟ That would be خربت. خربت.
rows.why: She said خربت السفرة / السفرة خربت (the get-form); he read 'I ruined' then 'she ruined' (39:47); she said that would be خرّبت, and he reached 'the trip was ruined?' (40:14) which she confirmed; his later production inti 5arrabti el-safra (41:10) was right.

rows.medi_said: who was made happy by us?
rows.why: انبسط is the get-form 'enjoyed'; he rendered it as the passive of the make-form; she repeated انبسط and he fixed to 'who enjoyed?' (42:33).

rows.medi_said: who was made happy or who enjoyed from us?
rows.why: He heard معنا as منا and read 'from us'; she recast 'With us. معنا' and he said 'whoops. I was saying mina' (42:47).

rows.medi_said: Uh, are you excited to a girl?
rows.why: تحمستِ is past; he read a present state 'are you excited'; she recast 'Did you get excited?' and he repeated it (43:25).

rows.medi_said: Why are you tired?
rows.why: ليش متعب؟ uses the active participle (sheet: tiring | Mut3eb | متعب vs tired | Ta3baan | تعبان); he read 'tired'; she repeated متعب and asked 'what's tired?' until he gave 'why is it tiring' (44:18); he never produced تعبان.

rows.medi_said: Not it as a don't be angry.
rows.why: He first read ما تتأسف as 'don't be angry' (تعصب); she repeated the word and he fixed to 'Oh, asaf. Don't apologize' (47:00).

rows.medi_said: uh, you guys don't, uh, don't be annoyed.
rows.right: sad / upset with him (ما تزعلوا منه)
rows.why: زعل is sad/upset, not annoyed (زعج); she queried 'Annoyed?' and he fixed to 'don't be sad from it or from him' (49:38-49:41).
rows.english: You all, don't be upset with him.

rows.medi_said: I enjoyed to it. No, Aloo, uh, Bill. Are you saying Bill? ... I got happy from him or to him?
rows.wrong: to it / from him or to him
rows.why: انبسط لـ means be happy FOR someone; he tried 'to it' and 'from him or to him'; she prompted 'Just the verb. I got happy له' then gave 'for him', he fixed (50:53).

rows.medi_said: You guys don't be annoyed.
rows.why: ما تزعجوه is the make-form with the -him ending; he read the get-form تنزعجوا; she said تزعجوه not تنزعجوا and stressed the ـوه (53:15) until he gave 'don't be annoying to him' (53:17).

rows.medi_said: They made us sad.
rows.why: The object ending ـني is 'me'; he read ـنا 'us'; she repeated زعلوني and he fixed to 'They made me sad' (54:24).

rows.medi_said: So it made me happy...
rows.amal_said: صح، it made happy، بس is it past or present؟
rows.why: بيبسطني carries the b-present; he read past 'made'; she asked past or present and he fixed to 'it makes me happy' (56:22).

rows.medi_said: you came. Aji, you said, "It makes me happy he came."
rows.amal_said: آجي. ... آجي. I come. It makes me happy like coming makes me happy in a, in a way.
rows.why: آجي is the I-form present; he read 'you came' / 'he came' (wrong person and tense); she recast 'آجي. I come' and he reached 'It's fun for me when I come?' (56:49), confirmed.
rows.english: It makes me happy that I come.

rows.medi_said: Did, uh, did you guys enjoy to me? Did you guys... I don't understand this one.
rows.amal_said: Great that you got the day part صح. They got-- they were happy for me. They got happy for me.
rows.wrong: did you guys enjoy to me
rows.why: انبسطولي is they-form + لي 'for me'; he read 'you guys ... to me'; she repeated it, he got 'they enjoyed...' and she gave 'they were happy for me', which he took (1:00:03).
